source_verification.claim: Heterozygous GFAP gain-of-function variants cause Alexander disease with astrocytic GFAP aggregation.
GFAP is a major astrocytic intermediate filament linked to Alexander disease.
Early-onset megalencephaly, seizures/spasticity and Rosenthal fibers are characteristic.

second_answer_attack.resolution: The pathology specifically describes Rosenthal fibers in astrocytes, which are associated with GFAP accumulation in Alexander disease. PLP1 causes Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease, arylsulfatase A causes metachromatic leukodystrophy, and alpha-synuclein belongs to synucleinopathies.
